title: Reservation Margin Trader and Tenant Fallback Runbook
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This doc sketches a pragmatic PRD/runbook hybrid for a feature set we call the Reservation Margin Trader (RMT). RMT is a capacity-management pattern for Dedicated pools that: (1) reduces wasted reserved capacity, (2) enables predictable short-duration bursts, and (3) enforces tenant isolation guarantees via soft fencing and graceful fallbacks. It’s intended to sit between rigid reservation models and fully opportunistic burst pools.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Customers buying Dedicated capacity complain about wasted headroom during off-peak and sudden latency spikes during microbursts.
- Current reserved model is binary: reserved vs on-demand. That forces overcommitment or frequent manual purchases.
- Simple burst credits are noisy: they either allow noisy neighbors or are over-conservative and waste margin.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce average unused reserved GPU minutes across participating pools by 25% within 6 months.
- Maintain 99.9% per-tenant p50 latency SLO for standard lanes, and ensure p95 degradation is predictable under contention (documented fallback path).
- Provide transparent cost accounting per token/second for any tenant using the RMT path.
- UX: customers can opt into a trade-off profile (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with clear descriptions and expected behavior.

Non-goals:
- Replace existing hard-reservations (commitment contracts) for enterprise legal billing. RMT is a capacity optimization layer on top of reservations, not a billing renegotiation engine.

Audience / personas:
- Platform Engineers at Redwood: need deterministic control and observability.
- Customer Platform/Infra owners: need clear guarantees and rollback knobs.
- SRE/Operations: need a runbook for when RMT misbehaves and affects SLOs.

Design summary (high level):
RMT introduces a circulating "margin" ledger for each dedicated pool. Each tenant has: a committed reserve (hard capacity), a margin allocation (fraction of pool reserved for soft trading), and a burst-credit balance. The RMT controller continuously trades margin: when a tenant has sustained underutilization, it can lend margin into a shared margin market for short-term credits to other tenants in the same pool. Lending tenants receive credits (discounted token price or bill credits) and reduced preemption risk for a configurable time window. Borrowing tenants consume credits and accept a soft-fence contract: their requests are routed through isolation lanes with higher preemption priority, and automatic fallback policies are enabled (model downgrade, reduced batch size, KV-cache use).

Key concepts and primitives:
- Margin Pool: a per-GPU pool construct representing the soft-servable capacity that can be traded.
- Margin Ledger: time-series per-tenant ledger of lent/borrowed capacity and credit issuance (for accounting and audits).
- Trade Window: configurable trade unit (e.g., 15m) where margin allocations can be rebalanced.
- Soft-Fence: a tenant-level throttling/priority tag. Soft-fenced workloads can be preempted faster but have lower cost, and explicit fallback routes.
- Fallback Lanes: pre-defined behaviors (model fallback, quantized variant, region reroute, deny with helpful error).

Autoscaling interaction:
- RMT coexists with autoscaling groups. Autoscaler continues to scale node count for baseline demand. RMT lives above that and handles microburst demand without requiring node-level scale-out for very short durations.
- When margin market is drained and demand persists beyond trade-window, autoscaler is signaled to scale up (with hysteresis tuned to avoid rapid node churn).

Routing and isolation controls:
- Traffic classifier marks requests with tenant RMT status (normal, borrowing, lending, soft-fenced).
- Router consults per-tenant policy: if borrower and pool under contention, route to pre-compartmentalized lanes with strict CPU/GPU share, KV cache priority adjustments, and an enforced timeout for fallback activation.
- Isolation enforcement uses cgroup-like runtime quotas and request admission controls; SLOs are tracked separately for each lane.

Accounting and pricing model:
- Credits minted when tenants lend margin; credits are redeemable as bill credits or token discounts. Credits are time-bounded (e.g., 30d expiry) and tied to ledger entries.
- Borrowers pay additional usage premium or consume credits; for customers on enterprise contracts, credits are converted to accounting notes for reconciliation.
- Transparency: console shows live ledger, projected cost savings, and worst-case fallback exposures.

Console/UX and API:
- New page: Pool Margin -> shows pool-level utilization, top lenders/borrowers, and trade-window heatmap.
- Tenant controls: toggle Opt-in, choose profile (conservative/balanced/aggressive), view current credits and pending trades.
- Admin controls: emergency quarantine (pause trading), manual buyback (force margin return), and audit log export.
- API: POST /v1/pools/{pool}/trade to request lending/borrowing; GET /v1/pools/{pool}/ledger for history.

Operational runbook (when things go wrong):
- Symptom A: p95 latency increase across pool and multiple tenants report timeouts.
  - Check Pool Margin dashboard for sudden borrower surge.
  - If borrow utilization > 85% and margin pool drained, toggle autoscale-signal and enable emergency quarantine.
  - If a single tenant dominates borrowing, escalate: mark that tenant for manual quarantine and refund ledger as appropriate.
- Symptom B: tenant reports unexpected preemption of high-priority jobs.
  - Verify tenant profile (was it set to aggressive?).
  - If incorrectly soft-fenced, manually remove soft-fence and reconcile recent ledger entries.
- Rollback path:
  - Disable trading globally (admin toggle) -> all margin returned to reservations -> re-evaluate SLO windows -> contact affected customers with remediation notes.

Metrics and telemetry to surface:
- Pool-level: margin utilization %, margin churn (trades/hour), time-to-autoscale signal, p50/p95 latency per lane.
- Tenant-level: credits minted, credits used, effective cost savings, preemption count, fallback invocation rate.
- Economic: incremental cost avoided (estimated GPU-minutes saved), credit liability outstanding.

Implementation roadmap (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiment, 6 weeks): instrumentation + read-only ledger + console prototypes. Small internal sandbox pool. (Owners: eng-applied-ml + infra)
- Phase 1 (private beta, 3 months): write-path for ledger, basic trade algorithm (conservative), simple fallback lanes, billing simulation. Pilot with 5 customers. (Owners: product-dedicated + eng-runtime)
- Phase 2 (public beta, 2 months): profiles, credit accounting, autoscaler integration, improved QoS gates. Expand pilot.
- Phase 3 (GA): SLA language updates, billing support, wider rollout, SRE runbooks finalized.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should lending incentives be? Discounts increase adoption but risk exposure. Requires modeling with historical utilization data (ENG-4122).
- Legal/billing: can credits be treated as discounts or must they be ledger-only for reconciliation? Requires Finance sign-off.
- Cross-pool trading: do we allow lending across pools in the same region? That complicates isolation guarantees. Start single-pool only.

Security and compliance considerations:
- Audit trail for all trades and ledger operations. Immutable export for a rolling 90d window.
- Encryption for ledger and trade metadata at rest. Keep PII out of ledger rows.

Appendix: quick algorithms
- Conservative matching: match lender offers to borrower demand by minimizing preemption risk (score = available-margin * historical-stability).
- Aggressive matching: maximize utilization by time-weighting short bursts (score = margin / expected-burst-duration).

Notes and references:
- See simulation spreadsheet linked in JIRA-ENG-4122 for modeled outcomes and sensitivity analysis.
- Related: review fallback-lanes design doc and autoscaler hysteresis RFC.

Action items (next steps):
- Data request: time-of-day utilization histograms per tenant for last 180d (owner: SRE).
- Prototype: allocate one dev pool and implement read-only ledger export (owner: eng-runtime).
- Legal: flag billing implications and draft credit policy (owner: finance).

End of runbook.
